title: ControlFusion: A Controllable Image Fusion Network with Language-Vision Degradation Prompts

predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The text states 'd(x) refers to the scene depth, estimated by DepthAnything-V2 [40]'. Reference [40] is 'Restormer: Efficient Transformer for High-Resolution Image Restoration' (Zamir, Arora, Khan, Hayat, Khan, Yang, CVPR 2022, pp. 5728-5739), a multi-task image-restoration transformer (deraining, deblurring, denoising). Restormer performs no monocular depth estimation. Depth Anything V2 (Yang et al., NeurIPS 2024, arXiv:2406.09414) is a distinct depth-estimation foundation model and does not appear anywhere in the reference list. Web verification of both papers confirms the cited reference does not support the attribution claim.

The text states 'We evaluate object detection performance on LLVIP to assess the fusion quality, using the retrained YOLOv8 [26]'. Reference [26] is 'You Only Look Once: Unified, Real-Time Object Detection' (Redmon, Divvala, Girshick, Farhadi, CVPR 2016, pp. 779-788), which describes the original YOLOv1 architecture. YOLOv8 is a distinct anchor-free detector released by Ultralytics (Jocher et al., 2023) and is not described in the 2016 paper; no Ultralytics reference is present in the bibliography. Web verification confirms YOLOv8 is a separate 2023 architecture (backbone/neck changes, anchor-free split head) that the 2016 citation cannot support.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section on DDL-12 dataset construction (Method) vs Section 5.1
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The RoadScene dataset is cited as [36] in the DDL-12 construction paragraph ('We selected 2,050 high-quality clear images from RoadScene [36], LLVIP [7], and MSRS [29] datasets') but as [35] in Section 5.1 ('we evaluate the fusion performance on four widely used datasets, i.e., MSRS [29], LLVIP [7], RoadScene [35], and FMB [16]'). Reference [35] is 'FusionDN' (Xu et al., AAAI 2020, which introduced the RoadScene dataset) while reference [36] is 'U2Fusion' (Xu et al., TPAMI 2022, which uses but does not introduce RoadScene). The same dataset is attributed to two different references within the same paper without explanation.

The paper reports selecting '2,050 high-quality clear images' and synthesizing 'degraded images with 12 types and 4 levels of degradation', yielding 'approximately 48,000 training image pairs and 4,800 test image pairs'. If each of the 2,050 images is degraded at 12 types x 4 levels = 48 variants, the total would be ~98,400 pairs (2,050 x 48), not ~52,800 (48,000 + 4,800). The stated pair counts correspond to ~1,100 source images (52,800 / 48), which is not reconciled with the stated 2,050 selected images.

The text states 'In terms of inference cost, CLIP and SFVA are responsible for a modest 0.81% and 7.5% of the total', but Table 8 shows these exact percentages are the FLOPs shares (13.088/1622.00 = 0.81% and 122.32/1622.00 = 7.54%), whereas the actual inference-time shares are 6.55% (0.0120/0.1833) and 3.66% (0.0067/0.1833). 'Inference cost' is conflated with FLOPs share; the time-based percentages differ substantially from the quoted values.

predicted_errors.error_location: Related Work figure (image_7.jpg) vs Figure 7 in Ablation Studies
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The Related Work section contains a figure rendered with alt-text 'Figure 7' (image_7.jpg), and a later figure is also numbered 'Figure 7: Visual results of ablation studies under degradation scenarios'. Two distinct figures share the same number 'Figure 7' — a numbering collision, possibly a markdown-conversion artifact but observable in the verified artifact.

summary: Exhaustive verification of ControlFusion (cs.CV, image fusion) over 64 snippets (27 text sections, 11 display equations, 15 figure references, 11 tables), routed to specialist verifiers at lenient strictness. Two high-confidence citation errors were confirmed against the published literature via web search: (1) the scene-depth estimator is cited as 'DepthAnything-V2 [40]', but reference [40] is Restormer (Zamir et al., CVPR 2022), an image-restoration transformer unrelated to depth estimation; Depth Anything V2 (Yang et al., NeurIPS 2024) is absent from the bibliography (confidence 0.92). (2) The object-detection evaluation uses 'the retrained YOLOv8 [26]', but reference [26] is the original YOLO paper (Redmon et al., CVPR 2016), which describes YOLOv1 and not the 2023 Ultralytics YOLOv8 architecture (confidence 0.88). A medium-confidence citation inconsistency: RoadScene is cited as [36] (U2Fusion) in the dataset-construction paragraph but as [35] (FusionDN, the actual origin) in Section 5.1 (confidence 0.75). Lower-confidence observations under lenient mode: the DDL-12 dataset arithmetic (2,050 images x 48 degradation variants = ~98,400 pairs vs. the stated ~52,800 total; the counts reconcile only with ~1,100 images, confidence 0.60); Appendix A.7 quotes FLOPs shares (0.81%, 7.5%) as 'inference cost' while the time shares are 6.55% and 3.66% (confidence 0.55); and two distinct figures share the label 'Figure 7' (Related Work placeholder vs. ablation results, confidence 0.50). Checks that PASS: all 11 display equations are mathematically sound, including the physics-driven degradation model (Eqs. 1-5), the cross-attention formulation, and the loss functions (Eqs. 10-14); all quantitative tables are internally consistent — ControlFusion's ablation rows in Table 6 exactly reproduce its composite-degradation rows in Table 2, the claimed SOTA in SD/VIF/Qabf (Table 1), the MSRS-nighttime/AWMM-100k claims (Table 3), the object-detection mAP@0.5:0.95 claim (Table 5), and the component shares in Table 8 (55.88%, 8.37%, 0.81%, 7.54%, 6.55%, 3.66%) all reconcile with the reported totals; no impossible or out-of-range statistics were found. The paper also transparently discloses the imbalanced pre-enhancement protocol behind Table 2. Because two findings carry confidence >= 0.85, the misattributed references must be corrected before the claims can be relied upon.
